extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent applicants/stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and practical guidance for conducting and scheduling applicant-examiner interviews (including WebEx/video conferencing) within the USPTO Patent Corps. Covers authorization, scheduling tools, preparation, WebEx operation, room reservation, and available resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews advance prosecution by explaining rejections and clarifying positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholder and examiner survey responses indicated that interviews explained rejections, discussed prior art, and clarified/better understood positions; stakeholders responded positively on questions regarding advancing prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use interviews to explain rejections, discuss relevant prior art, and clarify positions to advance prosecution. (Survey evidence supports interviews' effectiveness.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral authorization allowed for video conferencing (one-time per application)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Internet authorization policy was updated (MPEP § 502.03) to allow the applicant or representative to use only an Oral request to authorize a WebEx interview, in the same way they would request a telephone or in-person interview with the examiner, instead of submitting a written request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oral Authorization is for ONE TIME only within an application; if multiple video conferencing interviews are required, the applicant should give oral authorization for each video conference interview. See Fed. Reg. notice: 'Change to Internet Usage Policy to Permit Oral Authorization for Video Conferencing Tools by Patent Examiners' (80 Fed. Reg. 23787).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Automated Interview Request (AIR) form to schedule interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The AIR form is a way for applicants to schedule an interview using the Internet as an alternative to leaving an examiner voicemail. After submission, the examiner will respond to confirm the request or propose a new date/time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners may request additional information (e.g., an agenda) if one is not provided. The AIR form also provides a link to form SB/0439 for internet authorization. Applicants can find the AIR form on USPTO.gov (search 'AIR form') or via the interview practice website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request an agenda and familiarize with the application before the interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Interview preparation includes familiarizing yourself with the application which included requesting an agenda, reviewing the record, and consulting others if needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesting an agenda helps focus the interview; examiners should review the prosecution record and consult colleagues/SPE as needed prior to the interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: WebEx-specific preparation: scheduling, authorization, and early start
rubrics_metrics.description: WebEx tips included scheduling; obtaining written authorization; and starting the WebEx interview at least 15 minutes early.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule appropriately, ensure required (oral or written) authorization is in place, and begin the WebEx session at least 15 minutes before the interview to resolve connectivity/setup issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: WebEx operation proficiency (dialing-in, presenter controls, document sharing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Refresher training covered general reminders and tool review including dialing-in, becoming presenter, and document sharing. All examiners were trained/certified on WebEx starting in 2012 with refreshers and certification steps through 2015.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should be proficient in WebEx milestones (dial-in, switching presenter role, sharing documents) to run effective video interviews; SPE-conducted 1-on-1 certification was used previously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview principles: grant face-to-face and SPE participation requests normally
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO guiding interview principles state that all requests for face-to-face interviews by the applicant should normally be granted, and a request for SPE participation by the applicant will also normally be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that applicants often value in-person interviews as more productive; generally accommodate face-to-face requests and SPE participation unless there is a compelling reason not to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Interview Room usage and reservation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A Public Interview Room is a video conference room on each USPTO campus designated for Applicants to use to connect and collaborate with examiners working remotely or at a different USPTO campus. These are different from regular interview rooms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reservations for Public Interview Rooms must be made at least two business days prior to the interview; training covered internal procedures required to reserve a room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Interview Specialists and interview practice resources
rubrics_metrics.description: An Interview Specialist position has been created in each Technology Center (TC) to be a subject matter expert in interview practice and serve as a resource. A list of TC Specialists and additional resources are available on the USPTO interview practice website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the TC Interview Specialist for questions or assistance with interview practice; use the external interview practice website for forms, guidance, and links (e.g., AIR form, authorization forms).
